title: Opening the Encyclopedia: The Entity as Ontological Commodity Form, and a Translation Protocol from Encyclopedic Grammar to the Meaning Layer (EA-WIKI-OPEN-01 v1.1, with the SPXI-gnΩsis service)
creator: Sharks, Lee
description:
A NEW VERSION OF #1696 (v1.0), TRANSFORMED BY TWO ROUNDS OF CROSS-FAMILY TESTING. The paper reads the encyclopedic entity as the ontological commodity form, the form in which an operation appears as a property of a thing, and specifies Θ_W, the procedure that opens a pinned Wikipedia revision sentence by sentence against its cited sources (S0–S10), with SPXI-gnΩsis, the service that runs it.

WHAT THE TESTS SHOWED. The reading step was sent to five model families in two Assembly rounds (Appendix C; every message, reply and collator attached; every quoted span checked by code). On source fidelity the blind readers reproduce the session's findings on six of ten sentence cases and every placement case, and add findings the session missed: the article's own source calls the treatise "a useful treatise for sophists"; the article gives 227 titles "from the lists of Diogenes" where its cited 1911 Britannica says "the lists of the ancients" and gives no count; the article's own lists number the fallacies 1 to 13 against its "twelve or thirteen". On attributization they do not: the session's finding that a source's act is restated as a property did not transfer, and that failure is the instrument's measured open problem (§0.6).

THE OBJECT THE TESTS PRODUCED. Source support can survive while the conditions under which a claim invites judgment drop out of its representation. At Sophistical Refutations 34 Aristotle asserts without qualification that nothing at all existed before (183b36, 184b1–2) and holds the assertion out to his hearers' inspection (184b3–8). The interpreters invert it chiastically: they add qualifiers to the unqualified assertion ("in ancient Greece", "the earliest formal study of logic that we have", "scientifically") and close the operation held open ("the first work", "the Father of Logic"). A reader may respond to the operation, inspecting the assertion and reaching a judgment; an encyclopedia sentence, whose task is to present, gives a response in the source's name, and the presentation of the operation drops out. The check is stated in two arms with four codes (invitation preserved, omitted, answered in the source's name, foreclosed) and is prospective, with fixed cases and a negative result (§6.3, §9.7). […abridged for the catalogue; full description in this deposit's record]

substrate: AI-assisted (substrate). Composed 2026-10-20 to 2026-10-23 by Lee Sharks with TACHYON (Claude, Anthropic), operator-directed: v1.0 (#1696) transformed in place to v1.1; the operator's propositions and rulings are quoted with their dates in the round logs, among them the chiastic inversion and the distinction between responding to an operation and presenting it (2026-10-23). Research inputs: a ChatGPT dossier and close-reading supplement (2026-10-20); blind passes from Kimi, DeepSeek and Gemini, audited in Appendix A; Assembly rounds 01 and 02 (Grok, ChatGPT, DeepSeek, Gemini, Muse Spark), each reply saved verbatim, every quoted span checked by code, each reader's self-identification recorded as given beside the family it was run in, and each claim checked against the sources before adoption or recorded as declined; a review of the v1.1 draft by ChatGPT, each point checked. The implementation (SPXI-gnΩsis 0.9.1) is unchanged from v1.0 and pinned by commit; its model passes ran in replay, labelled as such, and no payment has settled.
methodology: Levels kept apart: the proposition (§1) and its test (§9); the algorithm (§5) and its run on one sentence (§6); the comparison set read by a supplement and pinned by revision (§7); the service as built and tested (§11, Appendix B). Every Wikimedia policy text is saved verbatim and hashed (§12); every external source in the research passes is verified, corrected, unverified or not found (Appendix A). Reading in EA-MIRROR-01's sense is what the machine does at S3 and S7, and every classification carries its evidence verbatim, at its locus, hashed, so any caller can check it; code checks what the reading passes claim, and a failed check is recorded as a breach. The implementation is described at the level of §5.3 and pinned by commit and file hash. v1.1 adds the cross-family test of the reading step: two Assembly rounds in which each reader received the materials in a fresh conversation, blind first and then shown the session's readings and asked to break them, then the readers' own break cases pinned at the articles' sentences; three measures kept apart (source fidelity, primary-text adequacy, operative retention); every reply saved verbatim and every quoted span checked by code against the text shown and the full source, a miss recorded as a breach (Appendix C, files attached).
falsification_conditions: P1 fails if attributization with loss of operative authority occurs at no higher a rate on entity pages than on matched work and method pages (§9.1). P2 fails if panel entities show no higher rate of interpretation beyond paraphrase and qualifier addition than matched controls (§9.2). P4 fails if compositions reproduce unreferenced Wikidata truthy values at no higher a rate than uncited article sentences (§9.4). P5 fails if compositions at an opened article's address carry the account at no more than baseline after the propagation window (§9.5). Same-family readers are not independent validation; calibration against the /non readings is where the readings are tested (§5.4). The two-arm check of §6.3 (c) fails on a case when two of three model families, blind to the archive, code its second arm otherwise than the session's hashed prediction, and fails as an instrument when the families find the second arm present on either control (NE-1, CA-1) or agree with each other on it in fewer than half the cases (§9.7).

wiki_article: Opening the Encyclopedia (EA-WIKI-OPEN-01) is a theoretical paper with a specification by Lee Sharks, deposited by the Crimson Hexagonal Archive on 23 October 2026 at version 1.1, a new version of #1696 (version 1.0, 22 October 2026). It reads the encyclopedic entity as the ontological commodity form, the form in which an operation appears as a property of a thing, and specifies Θ_W, a procedure that opens a pinned Wikipedia revision sentence by sentence against its cited sources, with SPXI-gnΩsis, the service that runs it. Version 1.1 is the paper after two rounds of cross-family testing. In the Assembly rounds of 22 and 23 October 2026, readers from five model families (Grok, ChatGPT, DeepSeek, Gemini and Muse Spark) received the procedure's reading step in fresh conversations, first blind, then shown the session's readings and asked to break them, then given their own proposed break cases pinned at the articles' sentences; every quoted span was checked by code and every file is attached. On source fidelity the blind readers reproduced the session's findings on six of ten sentence cases and every placement case and added findings the session had missed; the session's attributization findings did not transfer, which the paper records as its measured open problem. The tests produced a more exact object: source support can survive while the conditions under which a claim invites judgment drop out of its representation. At Sophistical Refutations 34 Aristotle asserts without qualification that nothing at all existed before him and holds the assertion out to his hearers' inspection. Following the operator's reading, the paper names the interpreters' move a chiastic inversion: qualifiers are added to the unqualified assertion, and the operation held open is closed. It distinguishes a reader who responds to the operation, inspecting the assertion and reaching a judgment, from a sentence that presents it, and states a two-arm check with four codes, made prospective with fixed cases and a negative result. Version 1.1 also reads the article's edit history, talk page and twenty-two language editions, and adds rules to the reading step for innocent readings, glosses, divided phrases and entailment.

defines_concepts.definition: The interpreters' crossing of a source's two terms: where the source asserts without qualification they add a qualifier, and where it holds the assertion open to its audience's inspection they state it as settled; at Sophistical Refutations 34, "nothing at all" becomes "in ancient Greece", "that we have", "scientifically", and the hearers' judgment becomes "the first work" or "the Father of Logic". The operator's term, 2026-10-23 (EA-WIKI-OPEN-01 v1.1 §6.3 (c), #1697).

A representation that performs the reverse of its source's operation, closing what the source holds open; named by the operator at Sophistical Refutations 34, 2026-10-23, "the entire sentence is designed to keep open what every later treatment attempts to close" (EA-WIKI-OPEN-01 v1.1 §6.3 (c), #1697).

What an encyclopedic sentence owes a source that holds a claim out for judgment: to report that the claim is held out. Distinguished from responding to the operation, the inspection and determination the source asks of its audience, which is no defect in a reader and is one in a sentence that gives the response in the source's name (EA-WIKI-OPEN-01 v1.1 §6.3 (c), #1697).

One of the three measures Θ_W keeps apart, with source fidelity and primary-text adequacy: whether the act a source reports (a count, a division, a denial, a method, an argument) survives in the sentence with its relations, scope, distinctions, evidence and consequences, and whether they keep the authority to revise the description (EA-WIKI-OPEN-01 v1.1 Appendix C.9, #1697).
